result.reasoning:
I could not refute it. The mechanism, the escape, and the consequence all reproduce; the one row the reporter names really does record the opposite of its own hypothesis.

WHAT IS TRUE (checked against the repo's own artefacts, not inferred)
1. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/sweep.py:142 (reporter said 143 — off by one, immaterial) is `locked = bool(re.match(r"\s*cs_(first|last)_(low|high)\d+\(", G["exprs"].get(vid, "")))`. `re.match` is anchored at the start of the string, so it fires on `cs_last_high20(...)` and misses `cs_rank(cs_last_high20(...))`, `cross_ema(cs_last_high20(...), 30)`, and the F114 expression. This is the only copy of the lock in the tree (grep over scripts/ and partura/).
2. runs/F114_q25_closeret/sweep_s3.json records for `h3_xfrozen_amtexp`: `"sign": -1.0`, `"sign_locked": false`, `"rank_ic_train": 0.00035568`, `utrain_long.long_ann -0.08226`, `long_sharpe -1.5267`, `train_long -0.10555 / -1.9424`. So the flip is a fact in the committed output, not a conjecture.
3. The batch-wide count: over all runs/*/sweep_*.json, 636 rows contain a cs_first_*/cs_last_* node, 624 have it at root (lock fires), 12 escape, and exactly 1 of the 12 chose sign=-1 — F114 h3_xfrozen_amtexp. (The reporter's 312/305/7 is a smaller file set; the decisive "1 chose -1" matches exactly.) The other 11 escapes (F101 h3_ov_kx_roll5, F110 h3_ov_xfroz_cvx/bkliq, F114 h3_xfr_plus_slowf/state/bdm, …) all already chose +1, so a fix is a no-op for them — no regression risk in this batch.

WHAT I REPRODUCED (real kernels — partura.ops_ext cs_last_high20/_lexi, alphacube cs_rank — and the real scoring path, partura.diagnose.ic_row + partura.books.books, i.e. exactly sweep.py::score; synthetic panels only)
4. The sign was decided by noise. With a pure-noise target over 975 train days (= train 20180102–20211231) and N=1000 on this panel shape, the median |mean daily rank IC| is 6.16e-04, 10–90 pct [2.10e-04, 1.80e-03], and the sign came out +1 in 9/20 worlds and -1 in 11/20. The real row's 3.56e-04 sits inside that no-signal band, and is ~50–100x smaller than its siblings' (k_known 0.0343, h3_xfr_own_slowf 0.0169). The recorded direction is a coin flip, not a measurement.
5. The full failure, end to end: in 14 worlds where the hypothesis is TRUE (screened names bleed, the joint top decile pays) and the full-cross-section IC is tuned to noise scale, the lock never fires, and the sign landed on -1 in 10/14. Those rows record long_ann -33% to -43% and long_sharpe -7.2 to -9.3, where the same panel with the sign locked to +1 records +52% to +60% and +12.0 to +14.0. The sign-flipped books hold 70–90% screened-out names; the +1 books hold 0.0%.
6. The two books are disjoint: overlap of the sign=+1 and sign=-1 decile long books is 0.0% of 100 names (it must be — they are the top and bottom decile of the same panel). So the recorded row is not a measurement of the hypothesis under any reading, independent of data.
7. In F114's own terms the flip is unambiguous. `h3_xfrozen_amtexp` = mul(cs_rank(LEG1), cs_rank(LEG2)) where LEG1 = `cs_last_high20(neg(slow), frozen)` is the locked sibling `h3_xfr_own_slowf` (sign_locked=true, +1, utrain +9.21%/+2.37) and both legs are written "higher = better" (the author put the `neg` INSIDE the screen's y argument precisely so the +1 lock would apply, the same pattern as `k_known_xfrozen`). The intended direction is therefore +1, and the "三件好事 / 若三者独立,这是 best_own 的天花板" claim in studies/F114_q25_closeret/hypo3.yaml (V group) was supposed to be read against +9.21%/+2.37. The table instead shows -8.23%/-1.53, which is the book of the names the screen exists to exclude. The hypothesis's own direction was never scored.

WHERE THE REPORTER OVERSTATES (corrections, not refutations)
8. Their quoted evidence "sign=-1 long book: 100/100 of the held names are screened-out ones" comes from tmp/review/screen-ops-universe/t1_lexi_ties.py [t2], which ranks the BARE `cs_last_high20` panel. The F114 expression multiplies two cs_ranks, which interleaves the blocks. Measured on the composed shape, the screened share of the sign=-1 book is 66.8% when the two legs are uncorrelated, and 39.2%–98.8% as corr(amtexp, frozen) runs from +0.8 to -0.8 — against 0.0% under sign=+1 at every correlation. Substance holds, the number does not.
9. "Print sign_locked in the output" is already half-done: sweep.py:145 writes `sign_locked` into the JSON. It is the human-readable table (sweep.py:233 and scripts/sweep_table.py:33) that prints `sign` but not `sign_locked`.
10. Blast radius is smaller than implied, and it is forward-looking: the flipped row did NOT reach the holdout (sweepfinal_s3.json carries h3_xfr_plus_slowf and h3_xfr_plus_state but not h3_xfrozen_amtexp), though scripts/sweep_final.py:109 (`sign = sign_ic if kind in ("base","bench") else float(R[k]["sign"])`) would have carried the flip into the holdout read had it been picked. And no committed F114 conclusion rests on it yet: handoff/F114_q25_closeret/STATE.md:90 and agents/verdict_adfbc90eeee4b463a.md both predate sweep_s3 (17:15/19:26 vs 18:02) and cite only s2 ids. So the damage is "one wrong row feeding the s3 synthesis that has not happened yet", not "a published conclusion to retract".

I could not verify the real +1 number — the panels live on the data box and are not persisted — so the magnitude of the correct F114 row is unknown. What is certain is that the recorded row measures a disjoint, oppositely-composed book.

One thing I noticed while scanning and did not report as part of this finding: sweep_s2.json and earlier have no `sign_locked` key at all (the lock postdates them), and in those files many ROOT-level screens carry sign=-1 (e.g. F102 seg_xfrozen_p, F103 seg_xfrozen_p, F101 h_rv_fold_drop_illiq). Those older tables have the same inversion on rows the current code would lock.

result.corrected_fix:
The finding stands; the suggested fix is right in effect but too blunt as a rule.

1. `re.search` instead of `re.match` is safe for the current batch (a no-op on all 11 other escapes, which already chose +1, and it corrects this one), but it is wrong as a general rule: it would also force +1 on an expression that deliberately reverses the screen — `neg(cs_last_high20(...))` ("hold only the flagged names"), or a composition where the screen's leg enters negatively, e.g. sweep's own `ov_m*` shape `add(cs_rank(A), mul(cs_rank(X_with_screen), -0.5))` or the second argument of a `sub`. Lock the direction only when it is actually determined:
   walk the tree with `partura.steer.parse_expr` and lock sign=+1 iff a `cs_first_*`/`cs_last_*` node sits on a SIGN-PRESERVING path to the root — no `neg` on the path, not the second argument of `sub`, no negative constant multiplier, and (conservatively) not inside a fold such as `abs_`/`pow_2` which destroys the ordering. If no such node exists, leave the sign to the IC as today. Both already-working families stay correct: `cs_last_high20(neg(y), x)` keeps its +1 (the `neg` is on y, below the screen, not on the path above it), and `sub(cs_rank(screen), pow_3(...))` keeps +1 (first argument of sub).

2. Fix the real cause of the flip too, not just the screen case. A direction chosen by a rank IC of 3.56e-04 — inside the no-signal band for this train length (measured median 6.16e-04, 10–90pct [2.1e-04, 1.8e-03]) — is a coin flip for EVERY variant, screen or not. In `score` (sweep.py:138), when |rank_ic| is inside that band, either score both signs and record both (`long_ann`/`long_sharpe` for +1 and -1, with `sign_ambiguous: true`), or pick the sign by the fit-split pure-long-book Sharpe, which is the selection criterion anyway and is what the half-life is already fitted on. Decide the sign by the thing the book is judged by, not by a statistic that can be noise.

3. Surface it. `sign_locked` is already written to the JSON (sweep.py:145); add it to the printed table at sweep.py:233 and scripts/sweep_table.py:33 next to `sign`, plus a marker for `sign_ambiguous`, so a reader sees which rows had their direction pinned and which had it decided by noise.

4. Guard the propagation path. scripts/sweep_final.py:109 carries a picked candidate's `R[k]["sign"]` forward to the holdout read unchanged. Have sweep_final refuse (or at minimum flag) a candidate whose `sign_locked` is false while its expression contains a screen node on a sign-preserving path — otherwise the next pick carries a flipped book into the only out-of-sample read you get.

5. Repair F114, scoped correctly. The panels are not persisted, so recompute just `h3_xfrozen_amtexp` on the data box and re-run `score` with the sign locked to +1. Compare it against its locked sibling `h3_xfr_own_slowf` (+9.21%/+2.37 utrain), which is the "two good things" baseline the V-group ceiling claim is about. Until that number exists, treat the V-group line in studies/F114_q25_closeret/hypo3.yaml ("若三者独立,这是 best_own 的天花板") as UNTESTED rather than refuted — not as a retraction, since no committed F114 conclusion cites the row yet (handoff/F114_q25_closeret/STATE.md:90 and agents/verdict_adfbc90eeee4b463a.md both predate sweep_s3 and cite only s2 ids). The repair belongs before the s3 synthesis, not after it.

6. Separately (not part of this finding, worth a pass of its own): sweep_s2.json and earlier have no `sign_locked` key — the lock postdates them — and in those files ROOT-level screens frequently carry sign=-1 (F102 seg_xfrozen_p, F103 seg_xfrozen_p, F101 h_rv_fold_drop_illiq, and others). Any s1/s2 conclusion read off those rows has the same inversion on rows the current code would lock.
